_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-29 14:26:55Z)**_

The short answer: DeadReckon has built much of the hard execution kernel, but it has not yet delivered the complete original experience.

Today it is a serious local verified-run system. It is not yet a dependable “start this goal, walk away, and trust it to keep working until the goal is genuinely complete” product.

## Where the project stands

| Original promise | Current state | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Define “done” before starting | Plain English can be compiled into `acceptance.yaml`; an LLM critic looks for weak checks and goals a stub could satisfy | Strong, although users can still fall back to detected project tests instead of consciously approving a real contract |
| Run coding CLIs in isolation | Git worktree and copy isolation are mature; changes require deliberate promotion | Strong for source isolation |
| Keep running until the goal is met | A normal run is foreground and limited to 12 turns; recovery normally requires `resume`. Chain has detached execution; current uncommitted plan work adds orphan adoption | Major remaining gap |
| Independently judge completion | A separate gate runs deterministic checks and validates the completion marker | Strong deterministic floor, but not the semantic meta-judge described in the original vision |
| Resist a dishonest worker | The worker cannot bypass a failing test merely by claiming completion; tamper checks catch several forms of weakening | Useful protection, but current “cannot forge” language overstates the boundary |
| Capture the whole run | State, snapshots, events, traces, spend, provenance, implementation notes and reports are persisted | One of the strongest parts of the system |
| Make the experience pleasant | The default five-command interface is quite good | Internally, too many execution models and advanced commands still leak into the mental model |

The most important correction is about the judge. The LLM currently helps write and critique the definition of done in [acceptance.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/acceptance.rs:642). Final acceptance is then deterministic. There is no independent LLM reading the original goal, the resulting change and the evidence and deciding whether the goal was semantically achieved.

That means the original `/goal` idea is only partly present: semantic judgment happens before execution, not at the final boundary.

The current run loop also has a real ceiling: normal runs configure 12 turns in [run.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/run.rs:496), after which the loop fails with a budget-exhausted state. State is durable, but the worker is not automatically durable. If its supervising process disappears, the job waits for an operator to resume or adopt it.

## What has genuinely been achieved

DeadReckon now has a credible “verified run” primitive:

1. Create an isolated workspace.
2. establish a completion contract;
3. run a chosen coding CLI;
4. retain state and evidence after every turn;
5. respond to gate failures with another corrective turn;
6. accept only after the external gate passes;
7. deliberately promote or export the result.

That is substantial. The current working tree passed the complete workspace test suite: 2,049 tests passed and none failed. I did not modify the repository.

The evidence system is also unusually thorough. [RunView](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/run_view.rs:20) gives a useful read model over persisted state and ledgers. The promotion boundary in [promotion.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/promotion.rs:25) makes “completed” meaningfully different from “applied to my repository.”

So this is not a speculative pile of commands. It contains a real, tested kernel.

## Necessary complexity

These are inherent to the product and should remain:

- Safely isolating and later promoting source changes.
- Supporting different CLI providers and their different streaming, cancellation and accounting behaviour.
- Durable job identity, state, locking, recovery and cancellation.
- Compiling acceptance criteria into executable checks.
- A semantic judge for requirements that cannot be reduced to tests.
- Preventing the worker from modifying its own acceptance mechanism.
- Recording enough evidence to explain why a result was accepted.
- Scheduling dependent and parallel units of verified work.
- Explicit budgets, deadlines and blocked states. “Until done” must not mean “loop forever.”

## Incidental complexity

This is complexity created by the current shape of the implementation rather than the underlying problem:

- Forty-five top-level command variants, even though most are hidden from ordinary help.
- Several overlapping journey concepts: run, chain, plan/fork/merge, campaign, reshape and others.
- Control truth spread across state JSON, several JSONL ledgers and sidecar files, requiring hand-written reconciliation and orphan adoption.
- Repeated provider, retry, narration and budget policies in different orchestration layers.
- Multiple documentation and narration pipelines.
- Compatibility aliases, no-op flags and old spellings.
- Making implementation-note production part of the completion ritual, rather than deriving the after-state account from captured evidence.
- Continuing to deepen campaigns, learning, narration and other secondary systems before unattended goal execution is fully dependable.

The architectural smell is: there is one good verified-run atom, but too many ways to arrange and supervise it.

## The trust-boundary problem

The README’s “it can’t fake the finish” claim is stronger than the current implementation warrants.

The gate nonce is stored inside the run directory, and the marker uses Rust’s `DefaultHasher` in [gate.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:752), rather than a cryptographic MAC or signature. General CLI-provider and Bash-tool execution do not consistently deny access to gate material. In addition, automatic sandbox selection can fall back to no sandbox.

The system can truthfully say:

> A separate process runs the acceptance checks, and an existing completion marker cannot make failing checks pass.

It cannot yet universally say:

> A hostile coding agent is technically unable to forge acceptance.

Results should distinguish:

- `VERIFIED + CONFINED`
- `VERIFIED + UNCONFINED`
- `NEEDS REVIEW`
- `FAILED`

That would make the confidence claim precise rather than absolute.

## Where I would take it next

### 1. Finish the durable goal executor

Make `deadreckon start` create a durable local job, return its ID and detach by default. A small supervisor or user service should:

- lease pending jobs;
- recover abandoned leases;
- restart after terminal or machine failure;
- retain bounded retry, spend and time policies;
- distinguish blocked, cancelled, budget-exhausted and failed;
- supervise runs, chains and plans through the same scheduler.

Temporal is the useful exemplar here. Its core model is a durable execution reconstructed from an append-only event history, with explicit lifecycle operations such as start, describe, result, cancel, terminate and reset. DeadReckon should extract those durability and operator-semantics patterns without becoming a distributed workflow platform. [Temporal workflow execution](https://docs.temporal.io/workflow-execution), [Temporal CLI workflow commands](https://docs.temporal.io/cli/command-reference/workflow).

### 2. Restore the semantic meta-judge as a second key

Completion should require:

1. Deterministic checks pass.
2. An independent, read-only semantic judge assesses the goal, contract, diff and evidence.

The semantic judge must never override failed deterministic checks. It should return `achieved`, `revise` or `uncertain`, with evidence-backed reasons. If it is unavailable in strict mode, the result becomes `NEEDS REVIEW`, not accepted.

This is necessary complexity: natural-language goals cannot always be completely compiled into tests.

### 3. Close the gate boundary

- Keep signing material outside the agent-visible workspace.
- Use HMAC-SHA-256 or a proper signature.
- Deny gate and proof paths across every provider and tool route.
- Bind the receipt to the contract, policy, source revision and resulting revision.
- Fail closed for unattended trusted runs.
- Add adversarial tests in which an agent deliberately searches for and attempts to forge the marker.

### 4. Collapse the product around one job model

Keep the ordinary surface:

```text
start
attach
status
list
finish
```

Plans, chains and campaigns should become internal scheduling shapes or an explicitly advanced namespace. They should all create the same durable jobs and verified-run receipts.

Similarly, create one append-only control event history and derive current state and `RunView` from it. Rich spend, trace and documentation evidence can remain separate, but lifecycle truth should have one source.

### 5. Freeze secondary expansion and dogfood the promise

Temporarily freeze deeper campaign features, learning/improve surfaces and additional narration variants. Test the core promise on 20–30 real tasks across multiple repositories and providers.

Measure:

- unattended verified completion rate;
- automatic recovery rate;
- false acceptance and false rejection;
- number of operator interventions;
- time required to understand the final result;
- supervision and judging cost.

Kill the terminal, worker and machine during these trials. Remove network access. Attempt to tamper with the gate. Run DeadReckon on DeadReckon itself.

## Bottom line

DeadReckon contains a strong, unusually well-tested verified-run kernel inside an overgrown product.

The next phase should not be more orchestration features. It should make one promise completely true:

> Give DeadReckon a goal and an approved definition of done. It will work in isolation, survive interruptions, stop for explicit bounded reasons, independently verify both the checks and the meaning of the result, and leave behind a clear receipt explaining what happened.

Once that experience is reliable and pleasant, the plans, chains and campaigns become valuable multipliers instead of competing product models.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-29 14:26:55Z)**_

“Finish the durable goal executor” means making DeadReckon responsible for the job after the user starts it.

Right now, DeadReckon has durable records, but not fully durable execution.

## Today

A normal run behaves roughly like this:

```text
Your terminal
    ↓
deadreckon run
    ↓
coding CLI
    ↓
gate
```

The `deadreckon run` process is the supervisor. While that process is alive, it keeps giving the coding CLI turns and checking the result.

DeadReckon saves enough state to recover, but:

- closing the supervisor stops the work;
- restarting the computer stops the work;
- someone must run `resume`;
- a normal attempt stops after 12 turns;
- detached execution exists for chains, but is not the common execution model.

That is resumable execution: “we can pick up where we stopped.”

It is not yet durable execution: “DeadReckon continues to own the job until it reaches a legitimate stopping point.”

## The proposed experience

The user should be able to do this:

```bash
deadreckon start "Add password reset"
```

DeadReckon would:

1. Create the isolated workspace.
2. Prepare and approve the definition of done.
3. Record a durable job.
4. Return a run ID immediately.
5. Let a background supervisor carry on.

```text
Started run dr-4821
Workspace: isolated
Status: running
Attach: deadreckon attach dr-4821
```

The terminal is no longer responsible for keeping the work alive.

```text
Terminal                 DeadReckon supervisor
   │                              │
   ├── start goal ───────────────→│
   │←── run ID ───────────────────┤
   │                              ├── run coding CLI
   │                              ├── save evidence
   │                              ├── run gate
   │                              ├── retry if appropriate
   │                              └── finish or stop explicitly
   │
   └── may close safely
```

`attach` would only observe or interact with the job. Disconnecting would not stop it.

## What keeps it durable

The background supervisor needs four basic mechanisms.

### A durable queue

`start` writes the goal into a local queue before execution begins:

```text
Job: dr-4821
Goal: Add password reset
Contract: acceptance.yaml
State: queued
Budget: $20
Deadline: 4 hours
Workspace: /path/to/worktree
```

If no supervisor is currently running, DeadReckon starts one.

### Leases and heartbeats

When a supervisor takes a job, it records:

```text
dr-4821 is leased by process 9312 until 14:35:00
```

It renews that lease periodically.

If the process crashes, the lease expires. Another supervisor can safely adopt the job. This prevents both abandonment and two supervisors working the same job simultaneously.

The uncommitted plan changes currently in the repository are moving towards this kind of orphan adoption, but it should become a shared facility for every execution shape.

### Checkpoints after every important event

DeadReckon already persists much of this. The durable executor would formalize events such as:

```text
Job started
Turn 1 started
Turn 1 completed
Gate failed
Corrective turn requested
Turn 2 completed
Gate passed
Semantic judge passed
Run verified
```

After a crash, the replacement supervisor reads this history and knows what to do next. It does not start the entire job again.

### Explicit stopping reasons

“Keep running until done” should not mean infinite retries.

A job may stop because it is:

```text
VERIFIED
BLOCKED — requires user decision
BUDGET_EXHAUSTED
DEADLINE_REACHED
FAILED — unrecoverable error
CANCELLED
```

Those states are part of the confidence model. Quietly dying because a terminal closed is not.

## It does not require a large distributed system

This could initially be a small local service:

```text
deadreckond
```

On macOS it could run through `launchd`; Linux could use a user-level `systemd` service. DeadReckon could also begin with a simpler detached conductor process, provided it has leases and automatic adoption.

It does not need Kubernetes, a server database or a cloud account. SQLite or an append-only local event log would be sufficient.

## Why this is the highest-priority gap

The original promise is not primarily “we save excellent records.” It is:

> Give the system a goal and trust it to carry responsibility for reaching a verified conclusion.

Without a durable executor, the human still carries part of that responsibility:

- keeping the process alive;
- noticing that it stopped;
- deciding whether to resume;
- restarting orchestration after a crash.

With it, the human only intervenes when DeadReckon produces an intentional `BLOCKED` state.

A practical definition of done for this feature would include:

- Start a run and close the terminal: it continues.
- Kill the coding CLI: DeadReckon retries or records a clear failure.
- Kill the supervisor: another supervisor adopts the run.
- Restart the computer: unfinished jobs resume automatically.
- Never run the same turn twice concurrently.
- Respect spend, time and retry limits.
- Preserve the same run ID, workspace and evidence throughout.
- Finish only through the normal verification boundary.

That change would turn DeadReckon from a well-persisted foreground runner into the “start it and trust it” product described in the original goal.

+pub(crate) const TRUSTED_SUPERVISOR_JOB_ID_ENV: &str = "DEADRECKON_SUPERVISOR_JOB_ID";
+
+fn trusted_supervisor_run_id(requested: Option<String>) -> Result<Option<String>> {
+    let Some(run_id) = requested else {
+        return Ok(None);
+    };
+    let trusted = std::env::var(TRUSTED_SUPERVISOR_JOB_ID_ENV).map_err(|_| {
+        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "--run-id is reserved for trusted supervisor launches".to_string(),
+        ))
+    })?;
+    if trusted != run_id {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "trusted supervisor job id does not match --run-id".to_string(),
+        )));
+    }
+    if run_id.len() != 32 || !run_id.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "trusted supervisor job id must be exactly 32 hexadecimal characters".to_string(),
+        )));
+    }
+    Ok(Some(run_id))
+}

+//! Durable local supervision for the first, single-leaf Watchkeeper slice.
+//!
+//! The append-only job history is control truth. Process exit is only a wakeup
+//! to inspect persisted run evidence; it is never accepted as completion.
+
+use std::ffi::OsString;
+use std::fs::{self, OpenOptions};
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+use std::process::{Child, Command, ExitStatus, Stdio};
+use std::time::Duration;
+
+use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
+use deadreckon_core::{
+    DeadreckonError, DeadreckonPaths, JobProjection, JobView, LeaseOwner, LeaseToken,
+    SupervisedProcess, append_fenced_job_event, claim_job_lease, heartbeat_job_lease, load_run,
+    pid_is_alive, read_supervised_process, spawn_grouped, validate_acceptance_marker,
+    write_supervised_process,
+};
+use deadreckon_protocol::{
+    Job, JobAuthority, JobEvent, JobEventKind, JobEventSequence, JobId, JobSchemaVersion, JobShape,
+    RunId, StopReason,
+};
+use serde_json::{Value, json};
+use uuid::Uuid;
+
+use super::course::{CourseShape, LaunchPlan};
+use super::run::TRUSTED_SUPERVISOR_JOB_ID_ENV;
+use super::super::{CliError, Result};
+
+const HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
+const LEASE_TTL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(15);
+const CHILD_METADATA_FILE: &str = "supervised-child.json";
+const SUPERVISOR_STDOUT_FILE: &str = "supervisor.out";
+const SUPERVISOR_STDERR_FILE: &str = "supervisor.err";
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
+struct SupervisorInstance {
+    owner: LeaseOwner,
+    executable: PathBuf,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
+struct LaunchInputs {
+    plan: LaunchPlan,
+    authority: JobAuthority,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug)]
+enum MonitoredChild {
+    Owned(Child),
+    Adopted(u32),
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug)]
+struct ChildExit {
+    status: Option<ExitStatus>,
+    adopted: bool,
+}
+
+pub(crate) async fn supervisor_serve_command(
+    once: bool,
+    requested_job_id: Option<String>,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
+    let instance = SupervisorInstance {
+        owner: LeaseOwner {
+            owner_id: Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
+            boot_id: boot_identity(),
+            pid: std::process::id(),
+            // Advisory only. Child process groups are persisted separately.
+            process_group: std::process::id(),
+        },
+        executable: std::env::current_exe()?,
+    };
+
+    loop {
+        let job_ids = match requested_job_id.as_deref() {
+            Some(job_id) => vec![job_id.to_string()],
+            None => eligible_single_job_ids(&paths)?,
+        };
+        for job_id in job_ids {
+            match supervise_one_job(&paths, &instance, &job_id).await {
+                Ok(()) => {}
+                Err(error) if requested_job_id.is_none() && live_lease_refusal(&error) => {}
+                Err(error) => return Err(error),
+            }
+        }
+        if once {
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+        tokio::time::sleep(HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL).await;
+    }
+}
+
+fn eligible_single_job_ids(paths: &DeadreckonPaths) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
+    let mut ids = Vec::new();
+    let entries = match fs::read_dir(paths.jobs_dir()) {
+        Ok(entries) => entries,
+        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(ids),
+        Err(source) => return Err(source.into()),
+    };
+    for entry in entries {
+        let entry = entry?;
+        if !entry.file_type()?.is_dir() {
+            continue;
+        }
+        let Some(job_id) = entry.file_name().to_str().map(ToString::to_string) else {
+            continue;
+        };
+        let Ok(view) = JobView::load(paths, &job_id) else {
+            continue;
+        };
+        if !view.projection.is_terminal() && view.job.shape == JobShape::Single {
+            ids.push(job_id);
+        }
+    }
+    ids.sort();
+    Ok(ids)
+}
+
+async fn supervise_one_job(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    instance: &SupervisorInstance,
+    job_id: &str,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let initial = JobView::load(paths, job_id)?;
+    if initial.projection.is_terminal() {
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    if initial.job.shape != JobShape::Single {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "supervisor leaf slice cannot execute {:?} job {job_id}",
+            initial.job.shape
+        ))));
+    }
+
+    let claim = claim_job_lease(
+        paths,
+        &initial.job.job_id,
+        &instance.owner,
+        Utc::now(),
+        LEASE_TTL,
+    )?;
+    let token = claim.token();
+
+    if let Some(child) = adoptable_child(paths, job_id)? {
+        append_control_event(
+            paths,
+            &token,
+            JobEventKind::ChildLinked,
+            format!("adopt-child:{}:{}", token.epoch, child.pid),
+            json!({
+                "run_id": job_id,
+                "pid": child.pid,
+                "process_group": child.pgid,
+                "adopted": true
+            }),
+        )?;
+        let exit = monitor_child(
+            paths,
+            &token,
+            MonitoredChild::Adopted(child.pid),
+        )
+        .await?;
+        return classify_persisted_attempt(paths, &initial.job, &token, exit);
+    }
+
+    // An attempt was durably started but no child identity survived. P6 cannot
+    // prove the old process group is dead, so fail closed instead of duplicating
+    // mutating work. P7 closes the smaller spawn-before-sidecar window.
+    if initial.projection.attempt_count > 0 {
+        append_attempt_stopped(
+            paths,
+            &token,
+            StopReason::LostContainment,
+            json!({ "reason": "attempt exists without adoptable child metadata" }),
+        )?;
+        append_terminal_event(
+            paths,
+            &token,
+            JobEventKind::Blocked,
+            StopReason::LostContainment,
+            json!({ "reason": "cannot prove the prior process group is dead" }),
+        )?;
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+
+    let launch = match load_launch_inputs(paths, &initial.job) {
+        Ok(launch) => launch,
+        Err(error) => {
+            append_terminal_event(
+                paths,
+                &token,
+                JobEventKind::Failed,
+                StopReason::CorruptHistory,
+                json!({ "error": error.to_string() }),
+            )?;
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+    };
+    let max_attempts = initial.job.policy.max_attempts.max(1);
+    for attempt in 1..=max_attempts {
+        append_control_event(
+            paths,
+            &token,
+            JobEventKind::AttemptStarted,
+            format!("attempt-started:{}:{attempt}", token.epoch),
+            json!({ "attempt": attempt, "run_id": job_id }),
+        )?;
+
+        match spawn_leaf(paths, &initial.job, &launch, &instance.executable) {
+            Ok((child, metadata)) => {
+                append_control_event(
+                    paths,
+                    &token,
+                    JobEventKind::ChildLinked,
+                    format!("child-linked:{}:{attempt}", token.epoch),
+                    json!({
+                        "attempt": attempt,
+                        "run_id": job_id,
+                        "pid": metadata.pid,
+                        "process_group": metadata.pgid,
+                        "adopted": false
+                    }),
+                )?;
+                let exit =
+                    monitor_child(paths, &token, MonitoredChild::Owned(child)).await?;
+                return classify_persisted_attempt(paths, &initial.job, &token, exit);
+            }
+            Err(error) => {
+                append_attempt_stopped(
+                    paths,
+                    &token,
+                    StopReason::FatalProvider,
+                    json!({ "attempt": attempt, "spawn_error": error.to_string() }),
+                )?;
+                if attempt < max_attempts {
+                    append_control_event(
+                        paths,
+                        &token,
+                        JobEventKind::RetryScheduled,
+                        format!("retry-scheduled:{}:{attempt}", token.epoch),
+                        json!({ "after_attempt": attempt, "reason": "spawn_failed" }),
+                    )?;
+                    heartbeat_job_lease(paths, &token, Utc::now(), LEASE_TTL)?;
+                    continue;
+                }
+                append_terminal_event(
+                    paths,
+                    &token,
+                    JobEventKind::Failed,
+                    StopReason::AttemptLimit,
+                    json!({
+                        "attempts": max_attempts,
+                        "last_error": error.to_string()
+                    }),
+                )?;
+                return Ok(());
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn load_launch_inputs(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job: &Job) -> Result<LaunchInputs> {
+    let plan_path = paths.job_launch_plan(job.job_id.as_ref());
+    let plan_digest = deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(&plan_path)?;
+    if plan_digest != job.launch_plan_sha256 {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "launch plan digest mismatch for job {}",
+            job.job_id
+        ))));
+    }
+    let plan = super::course::load_launch_plan(&plan_path)?;
+    if plan.shape != CourseShape::Single || plan.goal != job.goal {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "launch plan identity does not match single job {}",
+            job.job_id
+        ))));
+    }
+
+    let authority_path = paths.job_authority(job.job_id.as_ref());
+    let authority_digest = deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(&authority_path)?;
+    if authority_digest != job.authority_sha256 {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "authority digest mismatch for job {}",
+            job.job_id
+        ))));
+    }
+    let authority: JobAuthority = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&authority_path)?)?;
+    if authority.job_id != job.job_id
+        || authority.run_id != RunId(job.job_id.as_ref().to_string())
+        || authority.launch_plan_sha256 != job.launch_plan_sha256
+    {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "authority identity does not match job {}",
+            job.job_id
+        ))));
+    }
+    Ok(LaunchInputs { plan, authority })
+}
+
+fn spawn_leaf(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    job: &Job,
+    launch: &LaunchInputs,
+    executable: &Path,
+) -> Result<(Child, SupervisedProcess)> {
+    let job_dir = paths.job_dir(job.job_id.as_ref());
+    fs::create_dir_all(&job_dir)?;
+    let stdout = OpenOptions::new()
+        .create(true)
+        .append(true)
+        .open(job_dir.join(SUPERVISOR_STDOUT_FILE))?;
+    let stderr = OpenOptions::new()
+        .create(true)
+        .append(true)
+        .open(job_dir.join(SUPERVISOR_STDERR_FILE))?;
+    let mut command = build_leaf_command(paths, job, launch, executable);
+    command
+        .current_dir(&job.source_cwd)
+        .stdin(Stdio::null())
+        .stdout(stdout)
+        .stderr(stderr);
+    let (child, terminator) = spawn_grouped(command)?;
+    let metadata = SupervisedProcess {
+        pid: child.id(),
+        #[cfg(unix)]
+        pgid: Some(child.id()),
+        #[cfg(not(unix))]
+        pgid: None,
+    };
+    let metadata_path = child_metadata_path(paths, job.job_id.as_ref());
+    if let Err(error) = write_supervised_process(&metadata_path, metadata) {
+        let _ = terminator.terminate(Duration::from_secs(2));
+        return Err(error.into());
+    }
+    Ok((child, metadata))
+}
+
+fn build_leaf_command(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    job: &Job,
+    launch: &LaunchInputs,
+    executable: &Path,
+) -> Command {
+    let mut command = Command::new(executable);
+    command
+        .arg("run")
+        .arg(&job.goal)
+        .arg("--run-id")
+        .arg(job.job_id.as_ref())
+        .arg("--yes")
+        .arg("--quiet")
+        .arg("--plain")
+        .arg("--no-confirm")
+        .arg("--no-hints")
+        .arg("--prevent-sleep")
+        .arg("off")
+        .arg("--sandbox")
+        .arg(&launch.authority.sandbox_requested)
+        .arg("--max-spend")
+        .arg(effective_spend(job, &launch.plan).to_string())
+        .arg("--max-wall-seconds")
+        .arg(effective_wall_seconds(job, &launch.plan).to_string())
+        .env("DEADRECKON_HOME", paths.home())
+        .env(TRUSTED_SUPERVISOR_JOB_ID_ENV, job.job_id.as_ref());
+
+    let piece = launch.plan.pieces.first();
+    if let Some(provider) = piece
+        .and_then(|piece| piece.provider.as_deref())
+        .or(launch.plan.providers.coder.as_deref())
+    {
+        command.arg("--provider").arg(provider);
+    }
+    if let Some(model) = piece.and_then(|piece| piece.model.as_deref()) {
+        command.arg("--model").arg(model);
+    }
+    command
+}
+
+fn effective_spend(job: &Job, plan: &LaunchPlan) -> f64 {
+    plan.budget
+        .ceiling_usd
+        .map_or(job.policy.max_spend_usd, |plan_cap| {
+            plan_cap.min(job.policy.max_spend_usd)
+        })
+}
+
+fn effective_wall_seconds(job: &Job, plan: &LaunchPlan) -> u64 {
+    plan.budget
+        .wall_seconds
+        .map_or(job.policy.max_wall_seconds, |plan_cap| {
+            plan_cap.min(job.policy.max_wall_seconds)
+        })
+}
+
+fn child_metadata_path(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &str) -> PathBuf {
+    paths.job_dir(job_id).join(CHILD_METADATA_FILE)
+}
+
+fn adoptable_child(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    job_id: &str,
+) -> Result<Option<SupervisedProcess>> {
+    let path = child_metadata_path(paths, job_id);
+    let metadata = match read_supervised_process(&path) {
+        Ok(metadata) => metadata,
+        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(None),
+        Err(source) => return Err(source.into()),
+    };
+    Ok(pid_is_alive(metadata.pid).then_some(metadata))
+}
+
+async fn monitor_child(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    token: &LeaseToken,
+    mut child: MonitoredChild,
+) -> Result<ChildExit> {
+    loop {
+        let status = match &mut child {
+            MonitoredChild::Owned(child) => child.try_wait()?,
+            MonitoredChild::Adopted(pid) if !pid_is_alive(*pid) => {
+                return Ok(ChildExit {
+                    status: None,
+                    adopted: true,
+                });
+            }
+            MonitoredChild::Adopted(_) => None,
+        };
+        if let Some(status) = status {
+            return Ok(ChildExit {
+                status: Some(status),
+                adopted: false,
+            });
+        }
+        tokio::time::sleep(HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL).await;
+        heartbeat_job_lease(paths, token, Utc::now(), LEASE_TTL)?;
+    }
+}
+
+/// P5 will replace this intentionally small seam with one call to the combined
+/// receipt validator. Until then no persisted run can become `verified` here.
+fn classify_persisted_attempt(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    job: &Job,
+    token: &LeaseToken,
+    exit: ChildExit,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let exit_detail = exit_detail(&exit);
+    let state = match load_run(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()) {
+        Ok(state) => state,
+        Err(error) => {
+            append_attempt_stopped(
+                paths,
+                token,
+                StopReason::FatalProvider,
+                json!({ "exit": exit_detail, "state_error": error.to_string() }),
+            )?;
+            append_terminal_event(
+                paths,
+                token,
+                JobEventKind::Failed,
+                StopReason::FatalProvider,
+                json!({ "reason": "child exited without persisted run state" }),
+            )?;
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+    };
+
+    match state.status {
+        deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Completed => {
+            if let Err(error) = validate_acceptance_marker(&state) {
+                append_attempt_stopped(
+                    paths,
+                    token,
+                    StopReason::FatalGate,
+                    json!({ "exit": exit_detail, "gate_error": error.to_string() }),
+                )?;
+                append_terminal_event(
+                    paths,
+                    token,
+                    JobEventKind::Failed,
+                    StopReason::FatalGate,
+                    json!({ "reason": "persisted deterministic proof is invalid" }),
+                )?;
+            } else {
+                append_attempt_stopped(
+                    paths,
+                    token,
+                    StopReason::SemanticUnavailable,
+                    json!({ "exit": exit_detail, "run_status": "completed" }),
+                )?;
+                append_terminal_event(
+                    paths,
+                    token,
+                    JobEventKind::NeedsReview,
+                    StopReason::SemanticUnavailable,
+                    json!({
+                        "reason": "combined completion receipt validator is not available in this slice",
+                        "receipt_present": paths.job_receipt(job.job_id.as_ref()).exists()
+                    }),
+                )?;
+            }
+        }
+        deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Killed => {
+            append_attempt_stopped(
+                paths,
+                token,
+                StopReason::CancelRequested,
+                json!({ "exit": exit_detail, "run_status": "killed" }),
+            )?;
+            append_terminal_event(
+                paths,
+                token,
+                JobEventKind::Cancelled,
+                StopReason::CancelRequested,
+                Value::Null,
+            )?;
+        }
+        deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Failed
+            if state
+                .max_spend_usd
+                .is_some_and(|cap| state.total_spend_usd >= cap) =>
+        {
+            append_attempt_stopped(
+                paths,
+                token,
+                StopReason::SpendCap,
+                json!({ "exit": exit_detail, "spent_usd": state.total_spend_usd }),
+            )?;
+            append_terminal_event(
+                paths,
+                token,
+                JobEventKind::BudgetExhausted,
+                StopReason::SpendCap,
+                Value::Null,
+            )?;
+        }
+        deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Failed
+            if state
+                .max_wall_seconds
+                .is_some_and(|cap| state.total_wall_seconds >= cap) =>
+        {
+            append_attempt_stopped(
+                paths,
+                token,
+                StopReason::WallCap,
+                json!({ "exit": exit_detail, "wall_seconds": state.total_wall_seconds }),
+            )?;
+            append_terminal_event(
+                paths,
+                token,
+                JobEventKind::BudgetExhausted,
+                StopReason::WallCap,
+                Value::Null,
+            )?;
+        }
+        status => {
+            append_attempt_stopped(
+                paths,
+                token,
+                StopReason::FatalProvider,
+                json!({
+                    "exit": exit_detail,
+                    "run_status": serde_json::to_value(status)?,
+                    "failure_reason": state.failure_reason
+                }),
+            )?;
+            append_terminal_event(
+                paths,
+                token,
+                JobEventKind::Failed,
+                StopReason::FatalProvider,
+                json!({ "reason": "child exit was not backed by completed persisted evidence" }),
+            )?;
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn exit_detail(exit: &ChildExit) -> Value {
+    json!({
+        "adopted": exit.adopted,
+        "code": exit.status.as_ref().and_then(ExitStatus::code),
+        "success": exit.status.as_ref().map(ExitStatus::success)
+    })
+}
+
+fn append_attempt_stopped(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    token: &LeaseToken,
+    reason: StopReason,
+    extra: Value,
+) -> Result<JobProjection> {
+    append_control_event(
+        paths,
+        token,
+        JobEventKind::AttemptStopped,
+        format!("attempt-stopped:{}:{}", token.epoch, Uuid::new_v4()),
+        merge_stop_reason(reason, extra),
+    )
+}
+
+fn append_terminal_event(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    token: &LeaseToken,
+    kind: JobEventKind,
+    reason: StopReason,
+    extra: Value,
+) -> Result<JobProjection> {
+    append_control_event(
+        paths,
+        token,
+        kind,
+        format!("terminal:{}:{}", token.epoch, Uuid::new_v4()),
+        merge_stop_reason(reason, extra),
+    )
+}
+
+fn merge_stop_reason(reason: StopReason, extra: Value) -> Value {
+    let mut detail = match extra {
+        Value::Object(detail) => detail,
+        Value::Null => serde_json::Map::new(),
+        value => {
+            let mut detail = serde_json::Map::new();
+            detail.insert("detail".to_string(), value);
+            detail
+        }
+    };
+    detail.insert(
+        "stop_reason".to_string(),
+        serde_json::to_value(reason).unwrap_or(Value::String("corrupt_history".to_string())),
+    );
+    Value::Object(detail)
+}
+
+fn append_control_event(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    token: &LeaseToken,
+    kind: JobEventKind,
+    causation_id: String,
+    detail: Value,
+) -> Result<JobProjection> {
+    let now = Utc::now();
+    let projection = JobView::load(paths, token.job_id.as_ref())?.projection;
+    let sequence = projection
+        .last_sequence
+        .checked_add(1)
+        .and_then(JobEventSequence::new)
+        .ok_or_else(|| {
+            CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+                "job {} event sequence exhausted",
+                token.job_id
+            )))
+        })?;
+    let event = JobEvent {
+        schema_version: JobSchemaVersion::CURRENT,
+        job_id: token.job_id.clone(),
+        sequence,
+        event_id: Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
+        causation_id,
+        timestamp: now,
+        lease_epoch: token.epoch,
+        kind,
+        detail,
+    };
+    Ok(append_fenced_job_event(paths, token, now, &event)?)
+}
+
+fn live_lease_refusal(error: &CliError) -> bool {
+    error.to_string().contains("live lease held by owner")
+}
+
+fn boot_identity() -> String {
+    if let Some(value) = std::env::var_os("DEADRECKON_BOOT_ID")
+        && !value.is_empty()
+    {
+        return value.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
+    }
+    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
+    if let Ok(value) = fs::read_to_string("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id") {
+        let value = value.trim();
+        if !value.is_empty() {
+            return value.to_string();
+        }
+    }
+    format!("service-start:{}", Uuid::new_v4())
+}

+        let view = JobView::load(&paths, job.job_id.as_ref()).expect("visible job");
+        assert!(view.projection.is_terminal());
+        assert_eq!(
+            view.projection.outcome,
+            Some(deadreckon_protocol::JobOutcome::Failed)
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            view.projection.stop_reason,
+            Some(StopReason::AttemptLimit)
+        );
+        let history =
+            deadreckon_core::read_job_history(&paths.job_events(job.job_id.as_ref()))
+                .expect("history");
+        assert!(history.events().iter().any(|event| {
+            event.kind == JobEventKind::AttemptStarted
+        }));
+        assert!(history.events().iter().any(|event| {
+            event.kind == JobEventKind::AttemptStopped
+        }));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn root_run_uses_the_job_id() {
+        let temp = TempDir::new().expect("tempdir");
+        let (paths, job) = fixture(&temp, 1);
+        let launch = load_launch_inputs(&paths, &job).expect("launch");
+        let command = build_leaf_command(
+            &paths,
+            &job,
+            &launch,
+            Path::new("/opt/deadreckon"),
+        );
+        let args = command
+            .get_args()
+            .map(OsString::from)
+            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
+        let run_id_position = args
+            .iter()
+            .position(|arg| arg == "--run-id")
+            .expect("--run-id");
+        assert_eq!(
+            args.get(run_id_position + 1),
+            Some(&OsString::from(job.job_id.as_ref()))
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            command
+                .get_envs()
+                .find(|(key, _)| key == TRUSTED_SUPERVISOR_JOB_ID_ENV)
+                .and_then(|(_, value)| value),
+            Some(std::ffi::OsStr::new(job.job_id.as_ref()))
+        );
+    }
+
+    #[cfg(unix)]
+    #[test]
+    fn closing_start_parent_does_not_stop_job() {
+        let temp = TempDir::new().expect("tempdir");
+        let completed = temp.path().join("completed");
+        let mut command = Command::new("sh");
+        command
+            .arg("-c")
+            .arg("sleep 0.05; printf survived > \"$1\"")
+            .arg("deadreckon-supervisor-test")
+            .arg(&completed)
+            .stdin(Stdio::null())
+            .stdout(Stdio::null())
+            .stderr(Stdio::null());
+        let (child, _terminator) = spawn_grouped(command).expect("grouped child");
+        drop(child);
+
+        let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(2);
+        while !completed.exists() && Instant::now() < deadline {
+            thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));
+        }
+        assert_eq!(
+            fs::read_to_string(completed).expect("child survived dropped parent handle"),
+            "survived"
+        );
+    }
+}

+//! Trusted drivers that place existing orchestration engines under one Job.
+//!
+//! The driver specification is embedded in the signed launch plan. The
+//! mutable sidecar records which existing Plan or Campaign artifact belongs to
+//! the parent Job; it is navigation evidence, never completion authority.
+
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+use std::sync::OnceLock;
+
+use chrono::Utc;
+use deadreckon_protocol::{JobId, JobShape};
+use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
+
+use super::super::*;
+
+const DRIVER_SIGNAL: &str = "watchkeeper_driver";
+const DRIVER_STATE_FILE: &str = "driver.json";
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
+pub(crate) enum DriverKind {
+    Review,
+    FullPlan,
+    Campaign,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub(crate) struct DriverSpec {
+    pub(crate) kind: DriverKind,
+    pub(crate) child_count: Option<u8>,
+    pub(crate) apply: deadreckon_core::plan::ApplyWhen,
+    pub(crate) planner_provider: Option<String>,
+    pub(crate) child_provider: Option<String>,
+    pub(crate) child_provider_overrides: Vec<String>,
+    pub(crate) coder_provider: Option<String>,
+    pub(crate) reviewer_provider: Option<String>,
+    pub(crate) model: Option<String>,
+    pub(crate) source_init_git: bool,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub(crate) struct DriverState {
+    pub(crate) schema_version: u32,
+    pub(crate) job_id: JobId,
+    pub(crate) kind: DriverKind,
+    pub(crate) artifact_kind: String,
+    pub(crate) artifact_id: String,
+    pub(crate) recorded_at: chrono::DateTime<Utc>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
+struct DriverContext {
+    job_id: String,
+    acceptance_path: PathBuf,
+}
+
+static DRIVER_CONTEXT: OnceLock<DriverContext> = OnceLock::new();
+
+pub(crate) fn embed_driver_spec(
+    plan: &mut commands::course::LaunchPlan,
+    driver: &DriverSpec,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let mut signals = plan.signals.as_object().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
+    signals.insert(DRIVER_SIGNAL.to_string(), serde_json::to_value(driver)?);
+    plan.signals = serde_json::Value::Object(signals);
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn driver_spec(plan: &commands::course::LaunchPlan) -> Result<DriverSpec> {
+    let value = plan.signals.get(DRIVER_SIGNAL).ok_or_else(|| {
+        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "advanced job launch plan is missing its immutable driver specification".to_string(),
+        ))
+    })?;
+    serde_json::from_value(value.clone()).map_err(CliError::from)
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn driver_state_path(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job_id: &str) -> PathBuf {
+    paths.job_dir(job_id).join(DRIVER_STATE_FILE)
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn load_driver_state(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    job_id: &str,
+) -> Result<DriverState> {
+    let path = driver_state_path(paths, job_id);
+    Ok(serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(&path)?).map_err(
+        |source| {
+            CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::Json {
+                path: path.clone(),
+                source,
+            })
+        },
+    )?)
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn current_parent_job_id() -> Option<&'static str> {
+    DRIVER_CONTEXT.get().map(|context| context.job_id.as_str())
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn current_acceptance_path() -> Option<&'static Path> {
+    DRIVER_CONTEXT
+        .get()
+        .map(|context| context.acceptance_path.as_path())
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn record_current_artifact(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    kind: DriverKind,
+    artifact_kind: &str,
+    artifact_id: &str,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let Some(job_id) = current_parent_job_id() else {
+        return Ok(());
+    };
+    if job_id != artifact_id {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "advanced driver artifact {artifact_id} does not retain parent job identity {job_id}"
+        ))));
+    }
+    let state = DriverState {
+        schema_version: 1,
+        job_id: JobId(job_id.to_string()),
+        kind,
+        artifact_kind: artifact_kind.to_string(),
+        artifact_id: artifact_id.to_string(),
+        recorded_at: Utc::now(),
+    };
+    deadreckon_core::state::atomic_write_json(&driver_state_path(paths, job_id), &state)?;
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+pub(crate) async fn drive_job_command(job_id: String) -> Result<()> {
+    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
+    let job = deadreckon_core::load_job(&paths, &job_id)?;
+    if job.job_id.as_ref() != job_id {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+            "advanced driver job identity mismatch".to_string(),
+        )));
+    }
+    let plan = commands::course::load_launch_plan(&paths.job_launch_plan(&job_id))?;
+    let driver = driver_spec(&plan)?;
+    DRIVER_CONTEXT
+        .set(DriverContext {
+            job_id: job_id.clone(),
+            acceptance_path: commands::job::job_acceptance_path(&paths, &job_id),
+        })
+        .map_err(|_| {
+            CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
+                "this process is already driving another durable job".to_string(),
+            ))
+        })?;
+    std::env::set_current_dir(&job.source_cwd)?;
+
+    match driver.kind {
+        DriverKind::Review | DriverKind::FullPlan => {
+            if job.shape != JobShape::Graph {
+                return Err(driver_shape_error(&job_id));
+            }
+            drive_plan(&paths, &job, plan, driver).await
+        }
+        DriverKind::Campaign => {
+            if job.shape != JobShape::LegacyCampaign {
+                return Err(driver_shape_error(&job_id));
+            }
+            drive_campaign(&paths, &job, driver).await
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+async fn drive_plan(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    job: &deadreckon_protocol::Job,
+    plan: commands::course::LaunchPlan,
+    driver: DriverSpec,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let authority: deadreckon_protocol::JobAuthority =
+        serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(paths.job_authority(job.job_id.as_ref()))?)?;

+        DriverKind::Review => CliPlanMode::Review,

+        CliPlanMode::FullPlan => driver.child_count.unwrap_or(3),
+    };

+        seed_pieces: plan.pieces,
+        plan: PlanCommandArgs {
+            goal: job.goal.clone(),
+            n,
+            mode,
+            apply: driver.apply,
+            max_spend: Some(job.policy.max_spend_usd),
+            max_wall_seconds: Some(job.policy.max_wall_seconds as f64),
+            sandbox: Some(authority.sandbox_requested),
+            planner_provider: driver.planner_provider,

+async fn drive_campaign(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    job: &deadreckon_protocol::Job,

+) -> Result<()> {

+async fn dispatch_advanced_start_job(
+    args: StartCommandArgs,
+    decision: &StartLaunchDecision,
+    launch_plan: commands::course::LaunchPlan,
+    attach_flags: StartAttachFlags,
+    kind: commands::graph_job::DriverKind,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    if start_source_flags_present(&args)
+        || decision.source_fresh
+        || decision.source_from.is_some()
+        || decision.source_allow_dirty
+    {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
+            "source mode flags are only supported by start --mode run",
+            "omit source flags; graph jobs isolate their child workspaces internally",
+        )));
+    }
+    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
+    let cwd = std::env::current_dir()?;
+    let defaults = config_defaults(&paths)?;
+    let max_spend_usd = args.max_spend.or(defaults.max_spend).unwrap_or(10.0);
+    let max_wall_seconds = defaults.cli_max_wall_seconds.unwrap_or(36_000.0).max(1.0) as u64;
+    let sandbox_requested = defaults.sandbox.unwrap_or_else(|| "auto".to_string());
+    let provider_route = decision.provider_route.clone();
+    let graph = matches!(
+        kind,
+        commands::graph_job::DriverKind::Review
+            | commands::graph_job::DriverKind::FullPlan
+    );
+    let review = kind == commands::graph_job::DriverKind::Review;
+    let driver = commands::graph_job::DriverSpec {
+        kind,
+        child_count: decision.child_count,
+        apply: decision
+            .goal_shape
+            .as_ref()
+            .map(|shape| shape.apply)
+            .unwrap_or_default(),
+        planner_provider: (!review)
+            .then(|| {

+fn build_advanced_command(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job: &Job, executable: &Path) -> Command {
+    let mut command = Command::new(executable);
+    command
+        .arg("supervisor")
+        .arg("drive")
+        .arg(job.job_id.as_ref())
+        .env("DEADRECKON_HOME", paths.home());
+    command
+}
+
+fn attempt_detail(job: &Job, attempt: u32) -> Value {
+    if job.shape == JobShape::Single {
+        json!({ "attempt": attempt, "run_id": job.job_id.as_ref() })
+    } else {
+        json!({
+            "attempt": attempt,
+            "root_id": job.job_id.as_ref(),
+            "shape": job.shape,
+            "driver": "advanced"
+        })
+    }
+}
+
+fn child_link_detail(
+    job: &Job,
+    metadata: SupervisedProcess,
+    adopted: bool,
+    attempt: Option<u32>,
+) -> Value {
+    let mut detail = serde_json::Map::new();
+    detail.insert("adopted".to_string(), Value::Bool(adopted));
+    detail.insert("pid".to_string(), json!(metadata.pid));
+    detail.insert("process_group".to_string(), json!(metadata.pgid));
+    if let Some(attempt) = attempt {
+        detail.insert("attempt".to_string(), json!(attempt));
+    }
+    if job.shape == JobShape::Single {
+        detail.insert("run_id".to_string(), json!(job.job_id.as_ref()));
+    } else {
+        detail.insert("root_id".to_string(), json!(job.job_id.as_ref()));
+        detail.insert("shape".to_string(), json!(job.shape));
+        detail.insert("driver".to_string(), json!("advanced"));
+    }
+    Value::Object(detail)
+}

+fn needs_parent_receipt(

+            "artifact": artifact_kind,
+            "artifact_id": token.job_id.as_ref(),
+            "result_run_id": result_run_id,
+        }),
+    )?;
+    Ok(())
+}

+fn fail_advanced_attempt(

+    reason: StopReason,
+    message: &str,

+    append_terminal_event(

+        token,
+        JobEventKind::Failed,
+        reason,
+        json!({ "reason": message }),
+    )?;
+    Ok(())
+}

+async fn resume_plan(

+    driver: DriverSpec,
+) -> Result<()> {

+
+    let plan = deadreckon_core::plan::load_plan(paths, job.job_id.as_ref())?;
+    match plan.status {
+        PlanStatus::Merged => return Ok(()),
+        PlanStatus::Failed => {
+            return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+                "graph job {} has a failed plan and cannot be resumed automatically",
+                job.job_id
+            ))));
+        }
+        PlanStatus::Pending | PlanStatus::Forked => {}
+    }

+fn advanced_artifact_recoverable(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, job: &Job) -> Result<bool> {
+    if job.shape != JobShape::Graph {
+        return Ok(false);
+    }
+    let driver = match super::graph_job::load_driver_state(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()) {
+        Ok(driver) => driver,
+        Err(_) => return Ok(false),
+    };
+    if driver.job_id != job.job_id
+        || driver.artifact_kind != "plan"
+        || driver.artifact_id != job.job_id.as_ref()
+    {
+        return Ok(false);
+    }
+    let plan = match deadreckon_core::plan::load_plan(paths, job.job_id.as_ref()) {
+        Ok(plan) => plan,
+        Err(_) => return Ok(false),
+    };
+    Ok(matches!(
+        plan.status,
+        deadreckon_core::plan::PlanStatus::Pending | deadreckon_core::plan::PlanStatus::Forked
+    ))
+}
+
+fn schedule_advanced_recovery(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    token: &LeaseToken,
+    after_attempt: u32,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    append_attempt_stopped(
+        paths,
+        token,
+        StopReason::LostContainment,
+        json!({
+            "attempt": after_attempt,
+            "reason": "advanced conductor died; persisted graph is resumable"
+        }),
+    )?;
+    append_control_event(
+        paths,
+        token,
+        JobEventKind::RetryScheduled,
+        format!("advanced-recovery:{}:{after_attempt}", token.epoch),
+        json!({
+            "after_attempt": after_attempt,
+            "reason": "resume_persisted_graph"
+        }),
+    )?;
+    heartbeat_job_lease(paths, token, Utc::now(), LEASE_TTL)?;
+    Ok(())
+}

+fn finish_job_state(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    job: &deadreckon_core::JobView,
+) -> Result<deadreckon_core::PipelineState> {
+    if job.projection.outcome != Some(deadreckon_protocol::JobOutcome::Verified)
+        || job.projection.stop_reason != Some(deadreckon_protocol::StopReason::Verified)
+    {
+        let status = super::job::job_status_label(job);
+        return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
+            &format!(
+                "job {} is {status}; no verified receipt is available",
+                job.job.job_id
+            ),
+            &format!(
+                "deadreckon attach {}",
+                run_prefix(job.job.job_id.as_ref())
+            ),
+        )));
+    }
+    let state = load_run(paths, job.job.job_id.as_ref())?;
+    let receipt = deadreckon_core::validate_completion_receipt(paths, &state)?;
+    if !receipt.contained || receipt.sandbox_backend == "none" {
+        return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
+            &format!(
+                "job {} receipt does not prove contained execution",
+                job.job.job_id
+            ),
+            &format!(
+                "deadreckon attach {}",
+                run_prefix(job.job.job_id.as_ref())
+            ),
+        )));
+    }
+    Ok(state)
+}
